chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abi Ziyad al-Nahdi, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about pigskin that is made into a bucket with which water is drawn. He said: “There is no harm.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The correct way to understand this report is that there is no harm in drawing water with it, except that it is not permissible to use that water for wudu (ablution) nor for drinking. Rather, it is to be used for other than that, such as giving water to riding animals, livestock, and the like.

key_terms.جِلْدِ الْخِنْزِيرِ: pigskin used as the material of the bucket
key_terms.دَلْوًا: a bucket or vessel used for drawing water
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm in the stated act in this context
key_terms.يُسْتَقَى بِهِ الْمَاءُ: water is drawn by means of it

ai.seo_question: Can water drawn with a bucket made from pigskin be used for wudu (ablution) or drinking?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on using pigskin as a bucket for drawing water. The report states there is no harm in drawing water with it, while the compiler clarifies that the water thus drawn is not to be used for wudu (ablution) or drinking, but only for other uses such as watering animals.
